title: Pivotal Gateway: Hubframe navigation UX for compact rail and workspace switcher
creator: Lena Park
description: Problem: The Redwood Console's current left rail and workspace switcher create cognitive overhead for users who manage multiple projects and frequently jump between routes (dashboards, rollouts, cost views). Existing patterns either consume too much horizontal real estate or hide context when collapsed. Goal: Design a compact, telemetry-aware Hubframe navigation pattern that preserves route clarity, shows live cost/latency lenses at glance, and enables quick workspace switching with minimal disruption to task flow. Deliverables: Figma prototypes for three density modes (compact, standard, expanded), a routing mapping doc outlining URL semantics and deep-link behavior, annotation for accessibility and keyboard flows, usability test script and early results, rollout gating checklist for Console releases. Scope exclusions: tenant-level admin console redesign, mobile-first explorer (separate follow-up).
decisions: Primary rail will default to compact icons with hover-to-expand previews to balance horizontal real estate and discoverability.
Workspace switcher will use ephemeral inline previews (small snapshot card) rather than full context switch on hover to avoid accidental navigation.

Routing: each major Console surface (dashboards, rollouts, cost, models) maps to stable, human-friendly slugs (e.g., /app/{workspace}/dashboards) and supports deep links for panels and eval artifacts.
Telemetry lenses: integrate small cost/latency badges in the rail that update from existing Console telemetry streams; badges are off by default and opt-in per workspace.
Keyboard-first nav: Ctrl/Cmd+K opens command palette; dedicated shortcut Ctrl/Cmd+"\ toggles rail collapse for power users.
Accessibility: ensure expanded previews are focus-trap safe and provide descriptive aria-labels for each workspace and route item.
tradeoffs: Compact icon-first rail reduces visual clutter but increases initial discovery cost for new users; mitigated with on-boarding overlay and contextual tooltips.
Ephemeral previews reduce accidental context switch but add animation complexity and state management overhead for the frontend team.
Opt-in telemetry badges avoid noise for low-volume users but require additional backend gating and settings persistence work.
next_steps: Incorporate PM feedback from 2025-03-02 meeting and update Figma frames (Asha).
Hand off high-fidelity components and interaction specs to ENG for feasibility review (target sync 2025-03-10).
Run moderated usability sessions with 6 cross-functional console users and collect task completion/mental model notes (research to schedule by 2025-03-12).
Create a rollout plan with canary gating: beta opt-in workspace -> 10% orgs -> 50% -> full (owner-controlled toggle).
Add telemetry for 'switcher open', 'preview accepted', and 'route deep-link' events to evaluate impact on errors and latency.
acceptance_criteria: Figma prototype includes compact/standard/expanded rail states with annotated interactions and keyboard flows.
Routing doc specifies URL schema and behavior for deep-links, preserving back/forward semantics.
Usability report with at least 6 participants showing >80% success rate on 'switch workspace and open rollout' task or clear mitigation path documented.
Engineering feasibility sign-off on animation budget and state model documented in PR #7211.
Rollout checklist created with opt-in gating and telemetry events defined.
